rounds.title: Starter families

groups.label: Birds
groups.explanation: ROBIN, CRANE, EAGLE and SWAN are all birds. CRANE is also a lifting machine, but no machine group exists.

groups.label: Musical instruments
groups.explanation: FLUTE and OBOE are woodwind; CELLO and HARP are strings.

groups.label: Gemstones
groups.explanation: RUBY, OPAL and JADE are gemstones; PEARL is an organic gem formed inside a mollusc.

groups.label: Culinary herbs
groups.explanation: BASIL, THYME, SAGE and MINT are all herbs used in cooking.

rounds.explanation: Every term is used once in the intended partition. Categories and individual explanations are stored in groups.

redHerrings.rival: CRANE is also a lifting machine.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: There is no machine group, so CRANE can only complete the birds.

redHerrings.rival: SAGE is also a shade of green and a wise person.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No colour or people group exists; SAGE completes the herbs.

rounds.title: Everyday families

groups.label: Things with teeth
groups.explanation: A COMB, a SAW, a ZIP and a GEAR wheel all have teeth.

groups.label: Types of footwear
groups.explanation: BOOT, SANDAL, SLIPPER and TRAINER are all things worn on the feet.

groups.label: Words before ROOM
groups.explanation: BEDROOM, BATHROOM, CLASSROOM and SHOWROOM.

groups.label: Punctuation marks
groups.explanation: COMMA, COLON, DASH and FULL STOP are punctuation marks. FULL STOP is one tile.

rounds.explanation: Every term is used once in the intended partition. Categories and individual explanations are stored in groups.

redHerrings.rival: DASH also means to run quickly.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No movement group exists; DASH is the fourth punctuation mark.

redHerrings.rival: BOOT is also the luggage space of a car.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No car-parts group exists; BOOT completes the footwear.

redHerrings.rival: Editors must confirm a zip's teeth are a fair 'teeth' reading.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The interlocking elements of a zip are commonly called teeth.

fixtureHints.text: One category is Things with teeth.

rounds.title: Gentle families 1

groups.label: Kitchen utensils
groups.explanation: A WHISK, a LADLE, a SPATULA and a COLANDER are all kitchen utensils.

groups.label: Farm animals
groups.explanation: COW, SHEEP, PIG and GOAT are animals commonly kept on farms.

groups.label: Fruits
groups.explanation: APPLE, PEAR, PLUM and CHERRY are all fruits.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories. Every term belongs to exactly one of them.

rounds.title: Gentle families 2

groups.label: Weather
groups.explanation: RAIN, SNOW, HAIL and FOG are all kinds of weather.

groups.label: Planets
groups.explanation: MARS, VENUS, SATURN and JUPITER are planets of our solar system.

groups.label: Trees
groups.explanation: OAK, ASH, BIRCH and WILLOW are all trees.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories. Every term belongs to exactly one of them.

redHerrings.rival: ASH is also what remains after a fire.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No fire or weather reading fits; ASH completes the trees.

rounds.title: Gentle families 3

groups.label: Clothing
groups.explanation: A SCARF, a GLOVE, a JUMPER and a COAT are all things you wear.

groups.label: Sports
groups.explanation: TENNIS, GOLF, RUGBY and CRICKET are all sports.

groups.label: Colours
groups.explanation: RED, GREEN, PURPLE and YELLOW are all colours.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories. Every term belongs to exactly one of them.

redHerrings.rival: A green is part of a golf course.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: GREEN is not a sport; it completes the colours.

redHerrings.rival: A cricket is also an insect.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: There is no insect group; CRICKET completes the sports.

rounds.title: Gentle families 4

groups.label: Joints of the body
groups.explanation: The ELBOW, KNEE, WRIST and ANKLE are all joints.

groups.label: Rooms in a house
groups.explanation: KITCHEN, LOUNGE, STUDY and CELLAR are all rooms in a house.

groups.label: Sea creatures
groups.explanation: CRAB, SHARK, WHALE and OCTOPUS all live in the sea.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories. Every term belongs to exactly one of them.

redHerrings.rival: STUDY is also a verb meaning to learn.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No verbs group exists; STUDY completes the rooms.

rounds.title: Gentle families 5

groups.label: Dog breeds
groups.explanation: POODLE, BEAGLE, BOXER and LABRADOR are all breeds of dog.

groups.label: Shapes
groups.explanation: CIRCLE, SQUARE, TRIANGLE and OVAL are all shapes.

groups.label: Cheeses
groups.explanation: CHEDDAR, BRIE, STILTON and FETA are all cheeses.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories. Every term belongs to exactly one of them.

redHerrings.rival: A boxer is also a sportsperson.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: There is no sport group; BOXER completes the dog breeds.

rounds.title: Standard families 1

groups.label: Words before BALL
groups.explanation: FOOTBALL, SNOWBALL, BASKETBALL and MEATBALL.

groups.label: Card games
groups.explanation: SNAP, POKER, BRIDGE and RUMMY are all card games.

groups.label: Rivers in England
groups.explanation: The THAMES, SEVERN, TRENT and MERSEY all flow through England.

groups.label: In a sewing kit
groups.explanation: A NEEDLE, THREAD, a THIMBLE and a PIN are all found in a sewing kit.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a word-building category. Some terms could suit two groups; only one full partition uses every term.

redHerrings.rival: PIN forms PINBALL, so it could join the words before BALL.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The sewing kit has only four candidates (NEEDLE, THREAD, THIMBLE, PIN), so PIN must go there.

redHerrings.rival: A poker is also a fireplace tool.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No fireplace group exists; POKER completes the card games.

redHerrings.rival: BRIDGE could suggest rivers.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: A bridge is not a river; BRIDGE completes the card games.

redHerrings.rival: The Severn rises in Wales.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The label says 'in England', which the Severn satisfies for most of its length; editors should confirm.

rounds.title: Standard families 2

groups.label: Words after SUN
groups.explanation: SUNFLOWER, SUNBURN, SUNDIAL and SUNRISE.

groups.label: Flowers
groups.explanation: DAISY, TULIP, POPPY and LILY are all flowers.

groups.label: Playing card ranks
groups.explanation: KING, QUEEN, JACK and ACE are ranks in a pack of cards.

groups.label: Units of time
groups.explanation: A MINUTE, an HOUR, a WEEK and a DECADE are all units of time.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a word-building category. Some terms could suit two groups; only one full partition uses every term.

redHerrings.rival: FLOWER sits naturally beside the four flowers.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: FLOWER is not a kind of flower; it forms SUNFLOWER.

redHerrings.rival: A dial suggests a clock and therefore units of time.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: DIAL is not a unit of time; it forms SUNDIAL.

redHerrings.rival: MINUTE also means tiny.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No size group exists; MINUTE completes the units of time.

rounds.title: Standard families 3

groups.label: Words before BOARD
groups.explanation: CUPBOARD, KEYBOARD, SKATEBOARD and DARTBOARD.

groups.label: Birds of prey
groups.explanation: HAWK, FALCON, KESTREL and BUZZARD are all birds of prey.

groups.label: Currencies
groups.explanation: The EURO, POUND, DOLLAR and RUPEE are all currencies.

groups.label: Parts of a shoe
groups.explanation: The SOLE, HEEL, LACE and TONGUE are all parts of a shoe.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a word-building category. Some terms could suit two groups; only one full partition uses every term.

redHerrings.rival: SOLE is also a flatfish.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No fish group exists; SOLE completes the parts of a shoe.

redHerrings.rival: POUND is also a unit of weight and a verb.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No weights group exists; POUND completes the currencies.

redHerrings.rival: TONGUE is also a body part.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No body group exists; TONGUE completes the parts of a shoe.

rounds.title: Standard families 4

groups.label: Words after FIRE
groups.explanation: FIREWORK, FIREPLACE, FIREWOOD and FIREFLY.

groups.label: Insects
groups.explanation: BEE, WASP, MOTH and GNAT are all insects.

groups.label: Metals
groups.explanation: IRON, COPPER, TIN and LEAD are all metals.

groups.label: Imperial units of length
groups.explanation: The INCH, FOOT, YARD and MILE are imperial units of length.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a word-building category. Some terms could suit two groups; only one full partition uses every term.

redHerrings.rival: A fly is an insect, so FLY looks like a fifth insect.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: None of BEE, WASP, MOTH or GNAT forms a word after FIRE, so FLY (FIREFLY) must complete the FIRE group.

redHerrings.rival: A fire iron is a fireplace tool (two words).
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The FIRE group uses one-word compounds, and IRON is needed for the metals.

redHerrings.rival: LEAD is also a dog's leash.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No dog group exists; LEAD completes the metals.

rounds.title: Standard families 5

groups.label: Words before CAKE
groups.explanation: CUPCAKE, PANCAKE, FISHCAKE and CHEESECAKE.

groups.label: Fish
groups.explanation: COD, HADDOCK, PLAICE and TROUT are all fish.

groups.label: Parts of a castle
groups.explanation: The MOAT, TOWER, KEEP and TURRET are all parts of a castle.

groups.label: Shades of blue
groups.explanation: NAVY, TEAL, AZURE and COBALT are all shades of blue.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a word-building category. Some terms could suit two groups; only one full partition uses every term.

redHerrings.rival: FISH sits naturally beside COD, HADDOCK, PLAICE and TROUT.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: FISH is not a kind of fish; it forms FISHCAKE.

redHerrings.rival: PAN is a kitchen item.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No kitchen group exists; PAN forms PANCAKE.

redHerrings.rival: TEAL is also a duck.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No birds group exists; TEAL completes the shades of blue.

redHerrings.rival: KEEP is also a verb.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: A keep is the central tower of a castle.

rounds.title: Expert families 1

groups.label: Sound like letters of the alphabet
groups.explanation: SEA sounds like C, TEA like T, QUEUE like Q and WHY like Y.

groups.label: Trees
groups.explanation: YEW, ASH, ELM and FIR are all trees. YEW also sounds like U, but the trees need it.

groups.label: Birds
groups.explanation: JAY, KITE, SWIFT and ROOK are all birds. JAY also sounds like J, and ROOK is also a chess piece.

groups.label: Chess pieces
groups.explanation: KING, BISHOP, KNIGHT and PAWN are all chess pieces. The ROOK is needed by the birds.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: YEW sounds like the letter U.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The trees have only four candidates (YEW, ASH, ELM, FIR), so YEW must be a tree.

redHerrings.rival: JAY sounds like the letter J.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The birds have only four candidates (JAY, KITE, SWIFT, ROOK), so JAY must be a bird.

redHerrings.rival: ROOK is a chess piece.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The birds need ROOK, and KING, BISHOP, KNIGHT and PAWN fill the chess group.

redHerrings.rival: KNIGHT sounds like NIGHT.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: NIGHT is not a letter, so KNIGHT is not a letter homophone.

redHerrings.rival: TEA comes from a plant, and there is a 'tea tree'.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The tea plant is grown as a shrub and the tea tree is a different plant; editors should confirm TEA is not a fair fifth tree.

redHerrings.rival: A kite is also a toy.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No toys group exists; the red kite is a familiar British bird.

rounds.title: Expert families 2

groups.label: Facial hair
groups.explanation: MOUSTACHE, STUBBLE, SIDEBURNS and WHISKERS are all facial hair.

groups.label: Hide an animal
groups.explanation: BEAR is in BEARD, GOAT in GOATEE, COW (and OWL) in SCOWL and ANT in PLANT.

groups.label: Shades of green
groups.explanation: LIME, OLIVE, JADE and EMERALD are all shades of green.

groups.label: Citrus fruits
groups.explanation: LEMON, SATSUMA, GRAPEFRUIT and TANGERINE are citrus fruits. LIME is needed by the greens.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: A beard is facial hair.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only BEARD, GOATEE, SCOWL and PLANT hide an animal once GRAPEFRUIT is placed, so BEARD and GOATEE must go there.

redHerrings.rival: A goatee is facial hair.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for BEARD: the hidden-animal group needs it.

redHerrings.rival: GRAPEFRUIT hides APE.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The citrus group has only four candidates once LIME is a green, so GRAPEFRUIT must be citrus.

redHerrings.rival: A lime is a citrus fruit.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The greens have only four candidates (LIME, OLIVE, JADE, EMERALD), so LIME must be a shade of green.

redHerrings.rival: Lemon is also a shade of yellow.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Not green, so LEMON completes the citrus fruits.

redHerrings.rival: Cats have whiskers.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No cat group exists; whiskers are also hair on a man's face.

rounds.title: Expert families 3

groups.label: Add FISH to make one word
groups.explanation: SWORDFISH, STARFISH, JELLYFISH and SHELLFISH.

groups.label: Weapons
groups.explanation: A MACE, an AXE, a BOW and a DAGGER are all weapons. SWORD is needed for SWORDFISH.

groups.label: Astronomical objects
groups.explanation: A COMET, a PLANET, a METEOR and a NEBULA are all found in space. STAR is needed for STARFISH.

groups.label: Desserts
groups.explanation: TRIFLE, CRUMBLE, PAVLOVA and SORBET are all desserts. JELLY is needed for JELLYFISH.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: A sword is a weapon.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No other weapon forms a word with FISH, so SWORD must complete the FISH group.

redHerrings.rival: A star is an astronomical object.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No other astronomical object forms a word with FISH.

redHerrings.rival: Jelly is a dessert.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No dessert forms a word with FISH; the FISH group needs JELLY.

redHerrings.rival: Mace is also a spice.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No spice group exists; a mace is a club-like weapon.

redHerrings.rival: Rejected while authoring: SPEARFISH would have allowed a rival partition.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: SPEAR is not on this board.

redHerrings.rival: Rejected while authoring: MOONFISH would have allowed a rival partition.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: MOON is not on this board.

rounds.title: Expert families 4

groups.label: Hide a number
groups.explanation: NINE is in CANINE, EIGHT in FREIGHT, TEN in OFTEN and ONE in STONE.

groups.label: Imperial units of weight
groups.explanation: The OUNCE, POUND, TON and DRAM are imperial units of weight; a dram is a sixteenth of an ounce. STONE is needed by the hidden numbers.

groups.label: Teeth
groups.explanation: MOLAR, INCISOR, PREMOLAR and FANG are all teeth. CANINE is needed by the hidden numbers.

groups.label: Words before TRAIN
groups.explanation: EXPRESS TRAIN, SLEEPER TRAIN, STEAM TRAIN and GOODS TRAIN. FREIGHT is needed by the hidden numbers.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: A canine is a tooth.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only CANINE, FREIGHT, OFTEN and STONE hide a number, so each must go there.

redHerrings.rival: A freight train is a kind of train.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The hidden-number group needs FREIGHT; GOODS supplies the fourth train.

redHerrings.rival: A stone is an imperial unit of weight.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The hidden-number group needs STONE; DRAM supplies the fourth weight.

redHerrings.rival: TON is UK slang for a hundred.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: It does not hide a number word; it is a unit of weight.

redHerrings.rival: A dram is also a small measure of whisky.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: It is an established imperial unit of weight; editors should confirm it is familiar enough for Expert.

redHerrings.rival: Rejected while authoring: it hides EIGHT and would allow a rival partition with STONE.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Not on this board.

rounds.title: Gentle families 6

groups.label: Vegetables
groups.explanation: CARROT, PARSNIP, CABBAGE and LEEK are all vegetables.

groups.label: Road vehicles
groups.explanation: A BUS, TAXI, LORRY and VAN all carry people or goods along roads.

groups.label: Organs of the body
groups.explanation: The HEART, a LUNG, the LIVER and a KIDNEY are organs inside the body.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories of four. Each term belongs to exactly one group.

redHerrings.rival: A kidney bean is a vegetable.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: KIDNEY on its own names the organ, and the vegetables already have four members.

rounds.title: Gentle families 7

groups.label: Breakfast foods
groups.explanation: TOAST, PORRIDGE, MUESLI and a CROISSANT are common breakfasts.

groups.label: Jobs
groups.explanation: A NURSE, BAKER, PLUMBER and FARMER are all jobs.

groups.label: Seasons
groups.explanation: SPRING, SUMMER, AUTUMN and WINTER are the four seasons.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories of four. Each term belongs to exactly one group.

redHerrings.rival: A toast is also a speech made before drinking.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No speech or drink group exists; TOAST completes the breakfasts.

rounds.title: Gentle families 8

groups.label: Big cats
groups.explanation: The LION, TIGER, LEOPARD and CHEETAH are big cats.

groups.label: Drinks
groups.explanation: COFFEE, LEMONADE, COCOA and MILK are all drinks.

groups.label: Parts of a bicycle
groups.explanation: A bicycle has PEDALS, a SADDLE, a CHAIN and SPOKES in its wheels.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories of four. Each term belongs to exactly one group.

redHerrings.rival: A saddle also goes on a horse.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No horse group exists; SADDLE completes the bicycle parts.

rounds.title: Gentle families 9

groups.label: Months of the year
groups.explanation: MARCH, MAY, JUNE and AUGUST are months.

groups.label: European capital cities
groups.explanation: PARIS (France), ROME (Italy), MADRID (Spain) and LISBON (Portugal) are capital cities.

groups.label: British wild mammals
groups.explanation: The BADGER, OTTER, HEDGEHOG and SQUIRREL all live wild in Britain.

rounds.explanation: Three direct categories of four. Each term belongs to exactly one group.

redHerrings.rival: MARCH is also a verb meaning to walk in step.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No verbs group exists; MARCH completes the months.

redHerrings.rival: BADGER is also a verb meaning to pester.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No verbs group exists; BADGER completes the mammals.

rounds.title: Standard families 6

groups.label: Words before BOX
groups.explanation: POSTBOX, SHOEBOX, TOOLBOX and MATCHBOX.

groups.label: Hats
groups.explanation: A BOWLER, BERET, TRILBY and FEZ are all hats.

groups.label: Cricket terms
groups.explanation: In cricket the ball is bowled at the WICKET in sets of six called an OVER; a STUMP is one of the wicket's three uprights and the batter stands in the CREASE.

groups.label: Pasta
groups.explanation: PENNE, FUSILLI, LASAGNE and RAVIOLI are types of pasta.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a linguistic construction, with deliberate overlaps. Count the candidates for each group.

redHerrings.rival: A bowler is a cricketer, so BOWLER looks like a fifth cricket term.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The hats have only four candidates (BOWLER, BERET, TRILBY, FEZ), so BOWLER must be the hat.

redHerrings.rival: A cricket match.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: MATCH is not specific to cricket, and the BOX group has exactly four candidates, so MATCH completes MATCHBOX.

rounds.title: Standard families 7

groups.label: Words after HAND
groups.explanation: HANDBAG, HANDSHAKE, HANDCUFF and HANDRAIL.

groups.label: Parts of a shirt
groups.explanation: A shirt has a COLLAR, SLEEVES, BUTTONS and often a POCKET. CUFF is needed for HANDCUFF.

groups.label: Dances
groups.explanation: The WALTZ, TANGO, SALSA and FOXTROT are dances.

groups.label: Spices
groups.explanation: CUMIN, PAPRIKA, NUTMEG and CINNAMON are spices.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a linguistic construction, with deliberate overlaps. Count the candidates for each group.

redHerrings.rival: A cuff is part of a shirt.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No shirt part forms a word after HAND, so CUFF must complete HANDCUFF; the shirt keeps COLLAR, SLEEVE, BUTTON and POCKET.

redHerrings.rival: Salsa is also a spicy sauce, which suggests the spices.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Salsa is a sauce, not a spice; it completes the dances.

redHerrings.rival: SHAKE could suggest a dance move.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: It is not a named dance; it forms HANDSHAKE.

rounds.title: Standard families 8

groups.label: Words before LINE
groups.explanation: DEADLINE, HEADLINE, SKYLINE and FINISH LINE.

groups.label: Things with a crown
groups.explanation: A QUEEN wears a crown, a TOOTH has a crown (the part above the gum), a HAT has a crown (its top) and a WATCH has a crown (the winding knob).

groups.label: Snakes
groups.explanation: The COBRA, ADDER, PYTHON and VIPER are snakes.

groups.label: Scottish islands
groups.explanation: ARRAN, MULL, ISLAY and IONA are islands off the west coast of Scotland.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a linguistic construction, with deliberate overlaps. Count the candidates for each group.

redHerrings.rival: The crown is also the top of the head.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No other tile forms a word before LINE, so HEAD must complete HEADLINE; the crowns keep QUEEN, TOOTH, HAT and WATCH.

redHerrings.rival: SKY sounds like SKYE, a Scottish island.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The tile is spelt SKY, not SKYE; it forms SKYLINE.

redHerrings.rival: An adder is also something that adds.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No arithmetic group exists; the adder is Britain's native venomous snake.

rounds.title: Standard families 9

groups.label: Words after BOOK
groups.explanation: BOOKCASE, BOOKWORM, BOOKEND and BOOKSHOP.

groups.label: Gospel writers
groups.explanation: MATTHEW, MARK, LUKE and JOHN wrote the four Gospels of the New Testament.

groups.label: Nuts
groups.explanation: The ALMOND, CASHEW, PECAN and PISTACHIO are eaten as nuts.

groups.label: Sauces
groups.explanation: KETCHUP, GRAVY, PESTO and HOISIN are sauces.

rounds.explanation: Direct categories mixed with a linguistic construction, with deliberate overlaps. Count the candidates for each group.

redHerrings.rival: MARK forms BOOKMARK.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The Gospel writers have only four candidates, so MARK must go there; SHOP completes BOOKSHOP.

redHerrings.rival: Pesto is made with pine nuts.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Pesto is a sauce, not a nut; it completes the sauces.

rounds.title: Expert families 5

groups.label: Sound like numbers
groups.explanation: WON sounds like ONE, TOO like TWO, FOR like FOUR and ATE like EIGHT.

groups.label: Prepositions
groups.explanation: OVER, UNDER, ABOVE and BEYOND are prepositions of place. FOR is a preposition too, but the number sounds need it.

groups.label: Irregular past tenses
groups.explanation: SWAM, DRANK, FLEW and SANG are the irregular past tenses of swim, drink, fly and sing. ATE, WON and LET are needed elsewhere.

groups.label: Tennis terms
groups.explanation: In tennis LOVE is a score of nil, DEUCE is 40 all, a LET is a serve replayed after clipping the net and a VOLLEY is a shot played before the ball bounces.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: FOR is a preposition.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only WON, TOO, FOR and ATE sound like numbers, so FOR must go there.

redHerrings.rival: ATE is an irregular past tense (of eat).
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The number sounds need ATE; SWAM, DRANK, FLEW and SANG fill the past tenses.

redHerrings.rival: WON is an irregular past tense (of win).
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for ATE: the number sounds need it.

redHerrings.rival: LET is an irregular past tense (let, let, let).
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The tennis group has only four candidates (LOVE, DEUCE, LET, VOLLEY), so LET must be the tennis term.

redHerrings.rival: LOVE means nil, which looks like a number.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: It means zero but does not sound like a number word; it completes the tennis terms.

redHerrings.rival: DEUCE is an old word for two (dice and cards).
redHerrings.resolvedBy: It does not sound like a number word; DEUCE is needed by the tennis terms.

rounds.title: Expert families 6

groups.label: Hide a body part
groups.explanation: CHIN is in CHINA, HIP in SHIP, ARM in HARMONY and RIB in TRIBE.

groups.label: Countries
groups.explanation: PERU, CHILE, KENYA and NEPAL are countries. CHINA is needed by the hidden body parts.

groups.label: Boats
groups.explanation: A YACHT, CANOE, FERRY and BARGE are boats. SHIP is needed by the hidden body parts.

groups.label: Musical terms
groups.explanation: MELODY, RHYTHM, TEMPO and CHORD are terms from music. HARMONY is needed by the hidden body parts.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: CHINA is a country.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only CHINA, SHIP, HARMONY and TRIBE hide a body part, so each must go there.

redHerrings.rival: A ship is a kind of boat.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for CHINA: the hidden body parts need SHIP; BARGE completes the boats.

redHerrings.rival: Harmony is a musical term.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for CHINA: the hidden body parts need HARMONY.

redHerrings.rival: CHILE sounds like chilli.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: There is no food group; CHILE is a country.

rounds.title: Expert families 7

groups.label: Words before WORK
groups.explanation: FRAMEWORK, PATCHWORK, NETWORK and BRICKWORK.

groups.label: Fishing tackle
groups.explanation: An angler uses a ROD, REEL, HOOK and BAIT. NET is needed for NETWORK.

groups.label: Shades of red
groups.explanation: SCARLET, CRIMSON, MAROON and CHERRY are shades of red. BRICK is needed for BRICKWORK.

groups.label: Parts of a garden
groups.explanation: A garden may have a LAWN, POND, PATIO and flower BORDER. PATCH is needed for PATCHWORK.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: An angler's landing net is fishing tackle.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only FRAME, PATCH, NET and BRICK form a word before WORK, so NET must complete NETWORK.

redHerrings.rival: Brick red is a shade of red.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The WORK group needs BRICK; the reds keep SCARLET, CRIMSON, MAROON and CHERRY.

redHerrings.rival: A vegetable patch is part of a garden.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: The WORK group needs PATCH; the garden keeps LAWN, POND, PATIO and BORDER.

redHerrings.rival: MAROON is also a verb meaning to strand.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: No such group exists; maroon is a shade of red.

rounds.title: Expert families 8

groups.label: Hide a colour
groups.explanation: TEAL is in STEALTH, AMBER in CHAMBER, RED in SACRED and LIME in SUBLIME.

groups.label: Holy
groups.explanation: DIVINE, BLESSED, HALLOWED and SAINTLY all mean holy. SACRED is needed by the hidden colours.

groups.label: Wonderful
groups.explanation: SUPERB, SPLENDID, TERRIFIC and BRILLIANT all mean wonderful. SUBLIME is needed by the hidden colours.

groups.label: Words before POT
groups.explanation: JACKPOT, HOTPOT, TEAPOT and CRACKPOT. CHAMBER is needed by the hidden colours.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: SACRED means holy.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only STEALTH, CHAMBER, SACRED and SUBLIME hide a colour, so each must go there.

redHerrings.rival: SUBLIME means wonderful.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for SACRED: the hidden colours need it.

redHerrings.rival: A chamber pot.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for SACRED: the hidden colours need it; JACK, HOT, TEA and CRACK form one-word POT compounds.

redHerrings.rival: DIVINE can also mean wonderful.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: With SUBLIME and SACRED taken, the holy group has exactly four candidates (DIVINE, BLESSED, HALLOWED, SAINTLY), so DIVINE must be holy.

rounds.title: Expert families 9

groups.label: Sound like parts of the body
groups.explanation: HEAL sounds like HEEL, MUSSEL like MUSCLE, NAVAL like NAVEL and HARE like HAIR.

groups.label: Shellfish
groups.explanation: The CLAM, OYSTER, COCKLE and WHELK are shellfish. MUSSEL is needed by the body sounds.

groups.label: Put right
groups.explanation: To REPAIR, RESTORE, FIX or MEND something is to put it right. HEAL is needed by the body sounds.

groups.label: Of the sea
groups.explanation: MARINE, MARITIME, NAUTICAL and OCEANIC all describe things relating to the sea. NAVAL is needed by the body sounds.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: A mussel is a shellfish.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only HEAL, MUSSEL, NAVAL and HARE sound like body parts, so each must go there.

redHerrings.rival: To heal is to put right.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for MUSSEL: the body sounds need HEAL.

redHerrings.rival: NAVAL relates to a navy and the sea.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for MUSSEL: the body sounds need NAVAL.

redHerrings.rival: The cockles of the heart is a phrase about the body.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: COCKLE does not sound like a body part; it is a shellfish.

rounds.title: Expert families 10

groups.label: Words after MOON
groups.explanation: MOONLIGHT, MOONBEAM, MOONSHINE and MOONWALK.

groups.label: Shine with flashes of light
groups.explanation: To GLEAM, GLINT, SPARKLE or GLITTER is to shine with small flashes of light.

groups.label: Ways of walking
groups.explanation: To STROLL, AMBLE, STRIDE or MARCH are all ways of walking.

groups.label: Gymnastics apparatus
groups.explanation: The VAULT, RINGS, BARS and POMMEL HORSE are gymnastics apparatus.

rounds.explanation: Deliberate overlaps: several terms fit two groups, and only one complete partition uses all sixteen. Work from the groups with the fewest candidates.

redHerrings.rival: SHINE fits beside GLEAM, GLINT, SPARKLE and GLITTER.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: Only LIGHT, BEAM, SHINE and WALK form a word after MOON, so SHINE must complete MOONSHINE.

redHerrings.rival: LIGHT suggests the shining words.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for SHINE: the MOON group needs LIGHT.

redHerrings.rival: WALK is a way of walking.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for SHINE: the MOON group needs WALK; MARCH completes the ways of walking.

redHerrings.rival: The beam is gymnastics apparatus.
redHerrings.resolvedBy: As for SHINE: the MOON group needs BEAM; BARS completes the apparatus.
